findings.reason: the plan should extend the existing pagination contract to the remaining views and cite it, rather than describe a fresh one.
findings.text: §2 says "a list returns its highest-ranked rows up to a declared count, the total, and a cursor for the rest" as if new, but `paginate()` at reckon/mcp_views.py:2406 already returns exactly that (page, pagination with cursor/total) and `roadmap_view(` already takes `cursor` and `limit`, emits `pagination` and pages `wiring_findings` (reckon/mcp_views.py:3471, 3492-3496); §2, §3 and §7 cite none of it

findings.reason: §3 and §7 would become an extension of the existing parameter family rather than a new vocabulary the author must justify as parallel.
findings.text: §3 proposes that "every list view accepts `fields` with one shared vocabulary", but the crew tool already carries a `fields` request parameter end to end: reckon/mcp.py:2189 and :2174 pass `fields=` and `since=` into `serve_crew_view`, reckon/mcp_views.py:3851 forwards `fields=` to the velocity view, and reckon/mcp_views.py:4018 calls `project_live_rows(live_records, fields=fields, session=session)` (defined reckon/crew/query.py:174); the same is true of §7's `since` cursor (reckon/mcp.py:2174; the velocity view already accepts `since`/`until`/`fields`/`limit`/`cursor`, reckon/mcp_views.py:3846-3856)

findings.reason: naming the owner turns "add a vocabulary" and "add a cursor" into "widen the owner", which is the honest change and prevents a second field-projection path drifting from the first.
findings.text: §3's `fields` vocabulary and §7's `since` cursor duplicate the parameter/paging mechanism the crew-tool surface already owns; the owning code is the `paginate()` helper and the `serve_crew_view` request signature in reckon/mcp_views.py (with the row projection in reckon/crew/query.py:174 `project_live_rows`), and §5's "one owning function" for a run's classification is already owned by `classify_pointer` in reckon/crew/recovery.py (imported for the live view at reckon/mcp_views.py:1877)

findings.reason: §5 must say which existing parity guard it extends, or it will build a third one over the same facts.
findings.text: §5 leans on a parity test "from `a-project-reads-as-one-picture` §4" and cites it as the one to extend, but two parity mechanisms already exist in this tree: `tests/test_surface_parity.py` (rendered-vs-returned over the SPA parity harness) and `tests/test_producer_shares_the_classifier_verdict.py` (one run verdict across producer snapshots and emitted transitions); §5's own `plan-section-depends-on` lists `a-project-reads-as-one-picture#s4` but the section text names none of the three so a reader cannot tell which one carries the run-classification parity

findings.reason: the contract needs a machine-readable home (a per-view declaration the existing budget module or the test reads), otherwise nothing can fail when a view's declared size and its actual answer diverge.
findings.text: §2 says "every view declares a size contract in its docstring" and the contract is "met by shape", but the only thing that can enforce a contract is code: the ceiling is owned by reckon/mcp_budget.py (`response_ceiling`, `serialised_characters`), and a docstring promise is unreadable by any tool, so the declared contract sits beside the enforcement point rather than inside it

findings.reason: each adding section must account for its surface in its own text (what it replaces, merges, or why nothing can be), or the plan grows mcp_views and cli_options without bound.
findings.text: §4 adds a new MCP read `why(ref)` and a new CLI verb `reckon why`, §3 adds a `fields` request parameter to every list view, and §7 adds a `since` cursor to the brief, `crew live` and the roadmap; against public_definitions 1958, cli_options 393, mcp_views 16, refusal_families 23, no section names a definition it retires, a view it merges, or states why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §4's `why(ref)` hides the section graph, run placement, held paths and event join behind one ref argument, the smallest interface for the largest behaviour; the other sections add fields to views rather than modules.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 and §7 propose a `fields`/`since`/cursor vocabulary parallel to the one already owned by the crew-tool param family (reckon/mcp.py, reckon/mcp_views.py, reckon/crew/query.py), and §5's "one owning function" for a run's classification already has an owner to extend in reckon/crew/recovery.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1958, cli_options 393, mcp_views 16, refusal_families 23; §4 adds a new MCP read and a new CLI verb, §3 and §7 add request parameters, and no section names what it retires or merges or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2's paging, §3's `fields` and §7's `since` are all proposed as new but each already exists on the crew-tool surface (reckon/mcp_*), and the plan cites none of them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2's per-view size contract lives in a docstring, and a docstring is not readable by the tooling that would enforce it, so the contract is a promise beside the existing runtime ceiling in reckon/mcp_budget.py rather than an extension of it.
